resposta: Co-creation is aligning intent, emotion and action. In spiritual traditions, you participate in the creation of your reality along with something greater. In practice, nothing is created without action.
aprofundar: Inner reading: cocreating is not giving orders to the universe, it's not fighting it. The Tao Te Ching calls it wu wei, the effortless, forced action, like water surrounding a stone. The Dhammapada opens like this: the mind precedes all things. Practice: Write down an intention today, feel it in your body for a minute, and take a single concrete action in that direction before you go to sleep.
camada3: To contemplate: who is the self you want to co-create? If desire is born of fear, it creates more fear; if it is born of wholeness, it creates wholeness. The most subtle lesson is this: the highest work of co-creation is not what you achieve, it's who you become along the way.

resposta: The Law of Attraction says that like attracts like: thoughts and emotions would attract experiences. It comes from the 19th-century New Thought movement and was made famous by the 2006 film The Secret. There's no scientific proof that thinking alone attracts things.
aprofundar: Inner reading: what's real is that attention chooses what you see. He who searches for exits finds exits, persists more and does better. So the traditions speak of faith, but always along with works. Beware of the shadow of this idea: Never blame the sufferer for bringing his own pain. Practice: replace the request with the question, what step would I take today if I already trusted the path? And take the step.
camada3: To contemplate: the deepest attraction is not that of things, it is that of meaning. You become what you pay attention to every day. What, today, is getting your attention that you didn't choose?

resposta: Intention is the seed. A clear, written, repeated intention guides your attention, and attention guides your life.
aprofundar: Inner reading: In the tradition of the Upanishads it is said that you are your deepest desire, for as is the desire, so is the will, and as is the will, so is the act. Practice: Write the intention in the present, short and true, for example: I take care of my body every day. Read it when you wake up and when you sleep, and try it today with a little action.
camada3: To contemplate: behind every intention there is a deeper intention. Ask five times, why do I want that? In the fifth answer usually appears what the soul really asks for.

resposta: Visualizing is practicing in your mind. Athletes have been using it for decades: the mind trains the path before the body. Studies show that visualizing the process and the obstacles works better than visualizing the trophy alone.
aprofundar: Inner reading: Psychologist Gabriele Oettingen called it mental contrast: imagine the wish fulfilled, then the most likely inner obstacle, and the plan for when it will appear. The alchemists spoke of true imagination, the imaginatio, as the force that gives form. Practice: close your eyes for two minutes, see the outcome, see the obstacle, and say, "If this happens, I'll do that".
camada3: To contemplate: every visualization uses images that you already have. What can you still not imagine for yourself? There's your current limit, and your next growth.

resposta: Gratitude is the quickest shortcut to inner abundance. A grateful man sees what he already has.
aprofundar: Inner reading: Cicero wrote, in his Pro Plancio speech, that gratitude is not only the greatest of virtues, but the mother of all others. Gratitude shifts the center of the missing self to the receiving self. Research in positive psychology associates the habit of writing down gratitude with increased well-being. Practice: Tonight, write down three very specific things and in one of them, why it happened.
camada3: To ponder: Is it possible to be thankful for what has hurt you? Not for the pain in you, but for what she opened up in you. When gratitude reaches that point, it ceases to be technical and becomes state.

resposta: Affirmations are phrases that train the mind. They work best when they're believable to you and come with action. A 2009 study by Joanne Wood showed that exaggerated sentences can worsen the mood of those with low self-esteem.
aprofundar: Inner reading: the word only has power when the whole being agrees with it. If a statement sounds like a lie, the mind resists. In exchange I am rich because I am learning to take care of my money: a truth in the making convinces more than a fantasy. Practice: Write an affirmation that you can say by looking into your own eyes, in the mirror, without deviating.
camada3: To contemplate: the strongest affirmation is not about what you'll have, it's about who you are. I am, said silently, without anything afterwards, is one of the oldest phrases in contemplation.

resposta: In spiritual language, vibration is your inner state: what you feel and emanate. In physics, vibration is something else, measured in hertz, and the two should not be confused. There is no device that can measure the frequency of the soul.
aprofundar: Inner reading: what traditions call vibration is the quality of your presence. People feel when you're whole or divided. Raising the vibration, in practice, is taking care of sleep, body, company and thoughts. Practice: Before you enter a place today, take three breaths and choose the state you're going in.
camada3: To contemplate: you don't have to vibrate loud all the time. Serenity is not a peak, it's a bottom. What about you stays calm even when your moods go up and down?

resposta: Abundance starts as a mindset: seeing possibilities instead of just lack. But a mindset without strategy becomes just wishful thinking. Real prosperity comes from spending less than you earn, creating value and having patience.
aprofundar: Inside Reading: Jesus said, in Matthew six, where your treasure is, there your heart will be also. True poverty is when you never feel enough, even when you're full. Practice: Write down everything you spend for a week; abundance begins with clarity. And be wary of anyone who promises wealth in exchange for your money.
camada3: To contemplate: how much is enough? If you can't answer, you'll never get there. The highest abundance is needing little and having much to give.

resposta: Detachment is not giving up. It's about acting with total dedication and letting go of control over the outcome. Buddhism teaches that much of suffering stems from attachment.
aprofundar: Inner reading: In the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna says to Arjuna: You are entitled to action, but never to its fruits. This is not indifference, it is freedom: you do your best and do not enslave yourself to the result. Practice: pick something you control too much, an outcome, a person, an opinion, and do your part today and let go of the rest.
camada3: For contemplation, what would you be afraid to let go of? The answer shows where your prison is. It's not about losing what you love, it's about loving without holding on.
